First, to find ${A}^{2},$ we multiply $A$ by itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 20 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since ${A}^{3}={A}^{2}\cdot A,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{3} & ={A}^{2}\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 20 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-20 & -15 \\ 60 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
